economics.demand-analyse-1.0006.all: Income +5%: plant-based milk normal good, demand shifts right. Cheaper own-brand substitute: switching, demand for Meridian falls. Health campaigns: tastes shift towards it, demand rises. Net depends on strongest factor.

economics.demand-analyse-2.0001.all: Larger population = more consumers, demand shifts right. Young families: schools, childcare, children's goods, housing. New estates: transport, local shops. Prices may rise where supply slow to respond.

economics.demand-define1.0001.all: The amount of a product consumers are willing and able to buy at each price over a period of time.

economics.demand-define2.0008.all: A good for which demand falls when incomes rise (1), as consumers switch to better alternatives (1).

economics.demand-describe.0006.all: As price falls the product is more affordable (1) so consumers are willing and able to buy more (1).

economics.demand-diagram.0012.all: Complement cheaper, so demand for hot dogs shifts right to D1; P1 > Pe, Q1 > Qe.

economics.demand-explain.0015.all: Demand falls (1); higher income tax cuts disposable income (1); Halvoria households eat out less as restaurant meals are normal goods (1).

economics.economic-problem-analyse-1.000.all: Finite tax revenue vs unlimited wants (healthcare, education, roads), so government must prioritise; opportunity cost of each choice; growing 37m population makes scarcity worse; may raise taxes or borrow.

economics.economic-problem-analyse-2.000.all: Skilled labour shortage limits expansion and pushes up wages; raw materials +12% raise costs; lower margins or higher prices; may automate.

economics.economic-problem-analyse-3.000.all: Opportunity cost = next best alternative forgone: the job at EUR449/week (~EUR23,000/yr) over 3-4 years, plus work experience; fees and living costs add to sacrifice; future higher earnings may outweigh it.

economics.economic-problem-define1.0007.all: Natural resources used in production, e.g. minerals, soil, water.

economics.economic-problem-define2.0002.all: How to allocate finite/scarce resources (1) to satisfy unlimited wants (1).

economics.economic-problem-describe.0001.all: Resources are finite (1) so using them for one good means they cannot be used for another (1).

economics.economic-problem-explain.0015.all: Land is scarce (1); the field can grow only one crop at a time (1), so if Lucia grows maize she gives up the flowers (1).
